title: The Banach-Mazur rotation problem in finite dimensions: a transitive isometry group forces a Euclidean norm
abstract: A machine-checked proof that a finite-dimensional real normed space whose linear isometries act transitively on the unit sphere is Euclidean. This is the finite-dimensional case of the Mazur rotations problem, which appeared in Banach's 1932 book and is surveyed by Cabello Sanchez, Ferenczi and Randrianantoanina; its audience is the geometry of Banach spaces and their symmetries. It is the statement banach_mazur_rotation_problem.finite_dimensional of Formal Conjectures (BanachMazurRotation.lean), which marks it research solved. The result is classical and no priority is claimed. The proof takes the classical route: the isometries form a compact group, averaging a squared Euclidean norm over Haar measure gives an invariant quadratic form, and transitivity makes it a multiple of the squared norm. Mathlib has no topology on the isometry group, so the entry also builds it as a compact topological group with Haar measure. The general problem for separable Banach spaces, which Formal Conjectures marks research open, is not addressed.
